classification.difficultyReason: Each cubic requires selecting the taught integer-root search, reducing by division and recognising that the remaining quadratic needs exact formula solutions.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Solve $x^3-2x^2-6x+9=0$, expressing your answers in exact form.

answer.worked:
Let $P(x)=x^3-2x^2-6x+9$. Test factors of $9$:
$$\begin{align*}P(1)&=1-2-6+9=2\\P(-1)&=-1-2+6+9=12\\P(3)&=27-18-18+9=0.\end{align*}$$
By the factor theorem, $x-3$ is a factor. Divide by $x-3$:
$$\begin{array}{r|l}&x^2+x-3\\\hline x-3&x^3-2x^2-6x+9\\&\underline{-(x^3-3x^2)}\\&x^2-6x+9\\&\underline{-(x^2-3x)}\\&-3x+9\\&\underline{-(-3x+9)}\\&0\end{array}$$
Thus
$$(x-3)(x^2+x-3)=0.$$
By the null factor law, $x=3$ or $x^2+x-3=0$. For the quadratic:
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{-1\pm\sqrt{1^2-4(1)(-3)}}{2}\\&=\frac{-1\pm\sqrt{13}}{2}.\end{align*}$$
Therefore $x=3,\ \dfrac{-1\pm\sqrt{13}}{2}$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Solve $x^3-x^2-11x+3=0$, expressing your answers in exact form.

answer.worked:
Let $P(x)=x^3-x^2-11x+3$. Test factors of $3$:
$$\begin{align*}P(1)&=1-1-11+3=-8\\P(-1)&=-1-1+11+3=12\\P(3)&=27-9-33+3=-12\\P(-3)&=-27-9+33+3=0.\end{align*}$$
By the factor theorem, $x+3$ is a factor. Divide by $x+3$:
$$\begin{array}{r|l}&x^2-4x+1\\\hline x+3&x^3-x^2-11x+3\\&\underline{-(x^3+3x^2)}\\&-4x^2-11x+3\\&\underline{-(-4x^2-12x)}\\&x+3\\&\underline{-(x+3)}\\&0\end{array}$$
Thus
$$(x+3)(x^2-4x+1)=0.$$
By the null factor law, $x=-3$ or $x^2-4x+1=0$. For the quadratic:
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{-(-4)\pm\sqrt{(-4)^2-4(1)(1)}}{2}\\&=\frac{4\pm\sqrt{12}}{2}\\&=2\pm\sqrt3.\end{align*}$$
Therefore $x=-3,\ 2\pm\sqrt3$.
